title: Data visualization
planning: Define the canonical raw data shape and a pure transformation layer before implementing chart rendering.
Preserve machine timestamps and numeric values through sorting and filtering; format labels only at render time with an explicit timezone.
Do not fabricate smoothness by interpolating or backfilling across unknown periods unless the product semantics require it and the UI labels it.
Choose one chart implementation and remove abandoned variants after comparison.
Bound data volume and expensive transforms; derive data with memoization rather than mirrored state and JSON-stringify comparisons.
checks: Test unsorted data, duplicate timestamps, timezone and daylight-saving boundaries, market or business closures, gaps, empty series, and malformed values.
Test rapid symbol or range changes so stale responses cannot replace current data.
Render at narrow and wide dimensions and verify accessible text or tabular summaries for key values.
review: Reject sorting by formatted display labels, fake future prices, unnecessary animation, duplicate chart libraries, and test controls left in production UI.
Confirm tooltip values, axes, units, timestamps, and fallback provenance agree with the underlying data.
